flashcards.front: Why does adaptive bitrate (ABR) video transcode uploads into multi-bitrate 2–6 second `.m4s` GOP-aligned segments?
flashcards.back: Splitting into independent IDR-aligned segments lets players seamlessly switch between 360p, 1080p, and 4K mid-stream as bandwidth fluctuates, while making each immutable chunk 100% cacheable at CDN edge PoPs and pre-encoded in parallel via a DAG.

flashcards.front: What dual storage strategy keeps CDN hit ratios above 95% for massive VOD catalogs like Netflix?
flashcards.back: Serve the hot 5% zipfian head (new releases/trending shows) from NVMe/SSD Open Connect edge appliances directly inside ISPs, while storing the vast long tail in regional S3/origin shields fetched on miss.

quizzes.scenario: A creator uploads a 2-hour 4K master. Encoding it on one large worker takes 4 hours.
quizzes.question: How do streaming platforms cut that to minutes?
options: Lower the master's quality before encoding to save time
Encode only 1080p first and add the other bitrates on demand
Split at keyframes and encode the chunks in parallel workers
Use one larger GPU instance to encode the whole file faster
quizzes.explanation: Split the master at keyframe (GOP) boundaries into chunks of a few seconds, encode the chunks for every bitrate in parallel across many workers, then stitch the HLS or DASH manifests. Chunks are independent, so the work scales out.
optionExplanations: Lower input quality hurts every output and still runs serially.
This defers work but still encodes the main rendition sequentially.
Correct. Independent chunks turn hours into minutes.
A bigger machine helps a little but stays far slower than fan-out.

quizzes.scenario: Millions watch a trending series at prime time and regional ISP peering links fill up.
quizzes.question: How do large platforms keep most video bytes off the public internet?
options: Add more origin capacity in each region's data center
Switch delivery to peer-to-peer between nearby viewers
Lower the default bitrate for every viewer during prime time
Pre-load hot segments on caches placed inside ISP networks
quizzes.explanation: They place cache appliances inside ISP networks and pre-load popular segments there during off-peak hours. A control plane steers each client to the nearest appliance, so most bytes travel one hop inside the ISP.
optionExplanations: More origin capacity does not shorten the path through peering.
P2P is unreliable on mobile and is not how major services offload.
That cuts quality for everyone and still crosses peering links.
Correct. Bytes are served from inside the viewer's ISP.
